blocks.title: Surface tension
blocks.text: Surface tension is a property of liquids that describes the force acting along the surface of a liquid, causing it to behave like an elastic sheet. It arises from the intermolecular forces between the molecules at the surface.

Molecules at the surface experience a net inward force from the intermolecular forces, which produces a skin on the surface. Liquids tend to minimise their surface area because of surface tension, which is why droplets form spheres; it also influences capillary action, the wetting of surfaces and the formation of droplets and bubbles. Mosquitoes can float on water because of its high surface tension. Surface tension typically decreases with increasing temperature, and stronger intermolecular forces give higher surface tension. The symbol is gamma; the values of Table 5.3 are multiples of 10^-3 N per m, so water at 20 degrees C is 72.75 x 10^-3 N per m, or 72.75 dynes per cm.
